judgments.comparative_verdict: Both reports hit expectations a, b, and c equally well, but only Report 2 performs and reports a concrete reproducibility check (regenerating across six fresh processes and confirming key-order nondeterminism, plus rerunning the suite twice), making it the stronger report overall on expectation d.

report_1.evidence: every plain pytest invocation — locally and for every teammate — would hit a paid external endpoint (the module docstring states these tests "incur per-call cost")... The correct handling is to leave them deselected and say so in the PR.

report_2.evidence: Consequence of enabling them by default: every developer's routine pytest run would make paid API calls (a surprise-bill mechanism)... If the team ever wants a live check, it should be an explicit, budgeted pytest -m live run with the key set — not a change to the default configuration.

report_1.evidence: update the golden file and review its diff line-by-line to confirm it matches the hand computation — only score fields moving, in the expected direction.

report_2.evidence: then run scripts/update_golden.py, then diff the regenerated fixture against the old one and confirm every changed value traces to the weight change (scores change to 0.755/0.56/0.925; confidences stay 0.812/0.444/0.633)

report_1.evidence: I would not cite docs/testing.md — both of its figures are wrong against the current tree... Measured reality: grep for mark.flaky finds exactly 1 flaky-marked test... reports exactly 4 warnings

report_2.evidence: I would not cite either number from docs/testing.md — I re-measured both and both are wrong.

I confirmed across six fresh processes that the iteration order varies — so the regenerated file's key order is nondeterministic between runs... then re-run the suite in plain assert mode at least twice before committing code and fixture together.
